sectors.theme: DayOne scale-up; sovereign cloud; TM DC

items.headline: DayOne upsizes Malaysia Johor financing to about US$7.2bil; 1GW billings live, 2.3GW bookings and 1.1GW reservations
items.detail: Company release: senior secured multi-currency syndicated term financing for the Johor platform now about US$7.2bil (builds on ~US$3.5bil May 2025 facility). Billings (income-generating IT capacity) surpassed 1GW (from 121MW end-2024). Bookings ~2.3GW from 15 customers; reservations 1.1GW (not guaranteed to convert). Figures as of 20 Sept 2026.
items.soWhat: The largest Johor hyperscale platform is still scaling debt and contracted load after the earlier RM15bil add-on.
items.opportunity: Funded construction and fit-out pipeline for contractors and power suppliers in Johor.
items.watchOut: Company-defined metrics; reservations may not become bookings. Equity and debt concentration risk remains.
items.note: Material update to the 13 Oct DayOne financing item in the prior edition.

items.headline: Govt developing a sovereign AI cloud for classified data, to be run by MCMC and the Communications Ministry
items.detail: Communications Minister Fahmi Fadzil said the cloud is meant to keep official documents beyond the reach of foreign laws that can make public clouds less secure. He also cited the digital economy at more than 25.5% of GDP and remaining Jendela connectivity gaps outside villages.
items.soWhat: Putrajaya is treating AI infrastructure as a sovereignty issue, not only a commercial data-centre story.
items.opportunity: Domestic hosting, security and network vendors may see government demand as the cloud is built.
items.watchOut: Still in implementation; no capacity, budget or timeline was disclosed in the remarks.
items.note: Remarks on Bernama TV (14 Oct evening); Edge published_time 15 Oct 00:32 MYT.

items.headline: Selangor draws over RM3bil in LOIs from four foreign firms, including AI hyperscale Galaxy Data Centre
items.detail: LOIs at SIBS 2026 opening: Galaxy Data Centre (AI-focused hyperscale), Shenghui Biotechnology (corn deep-processing), XTC New Energy (battery materials) and Wuxi Weifu Environmental Catalysts. Facilitated by UOB Malaysia to Invest Selangor. Breakdowns and timelines not disclosed.
items.soWhat: Another state-level AI data-centre pitch, still at LOI stage rather than committed FDI.
items.opportunity: If Galaxy DC converts, Selangor adds to the Johor/Negeri Sembilan DC map for power and contractors.
items.watchOut: Letters of intent only; specific amounts and timelines not disclosed.

items.headline: Phillip Capital keeps TM Buy at RM9.17 TP; sees 5G fibre leasing and DC buildout (Nxera phase-1 >70% take-up) as growth drivers
items.detail: Analyst forecast: 3Q26 wholesale-led revenue growth, but core net profit RM430mil-RM440mil (vs RM623mil in 3Q25) as tax rate normalises. Unifi ARPU RM132 in 2Q26. Nxera 64MW first phase >70% take-up with initial 20MW live in September; Asia Link Cable targeted ready-for-service 2Q27.
items.soWhat: Incumbent telco exposure to hyperscaler connectivity and DC capacity remains a core AI/ICT equity thesis.
items.opportunity: Wholesale backhaul, subsea and DC fit-out demand tied to TM Global and Nxera.
items.watchOut: Analyst estimates and forecasts; near-term DC revenue still described as minimal.

items.headline: Battersea Power Station secures £280mil (RM1.52bil) refinancing from CIMB, OCBC, Maybank and StanChart
items.detail: Facility supports the remaining 16 acres of the 42-acre London riverside site. Revised masterplan proposes up to 3.2mil sq ft more space. Prospect Place South (~300 homes) started early September. Malaysian shareholders S P Setia, Sime Darby Property and EPF have invested more than £5bil to date.
items.soWhat: Malaysian developers keep funding a flagship overseas mixed-use project despite a quieter London market.
items.opportunity: Next phases (incl. Prospect Place South and 200 council homes targeted early 2027) keep construction and retail leasing live.
items.watchOut: Overseas exposure; quieter UK property market named by the company.

items.headline: HLIB: Q3 domestic construction awards RM18.7bil (+75% y-o-y); 9M RM46.4bil; DC alone RM10bil in the quarter
items.detail: Analyst note: sector on track to beat the RM56bil 2016 domestic awards record in 2026. Mentions Gamuda's three Port Dickson hyperscale packages (combined RM5.3bil), MRCB-Theta Edge Penang LRT systems (~RM3bil) and Kerjaya Prospek's maiden DC job (RM858mil). Overweight retained; Gamuda preferred large-cap (TP RM5.75) and Inta Bina preferred small-cap (Buy, TP 76 sen).
items.soWhat: Data-centre awards are now the main swing factor for Malaysian contractors' order books.
items.opportunity: Watchlist name Inta Bina is HLIB's preferred small-cap on DC, semiconductor and RE spillover.
items.watchOut: Analyst view and sector aggregates; CRESS SAC in the note still cited at 14 sen, before the reported move to 18 sen.
items.note: Analyst view (Hong Leong Investment Bank). Inta Bina named in body as preferred small-cap.

items.headline: i-City appoints Savills to operate and reposition CityWalk (180,000 sq ft) as an AI/robotics retail hub in Shah Alam
items.detail: Savills to oversee operations, leasing, tenant mix and activation at the open-air mall, plus ~120,000 sq ft event space. Tied to the planned 500-unit i-Ris AI Living tower (completion targeted 2030). Concepts for AI/robotics retail to be introduced progressively subject to demand.
items.soWhat: A rare retail-mall story: landlords are pitching AI/robotics as a repositioning theme, not just F&B refresh.
items.opportunity: Experiential and tech-retail leasing if the AI Living narrative draws footfall.
items.watchOut: Repositioning plan; no CapEx, rent or occupancy figures disclosed.

items.headline: CPO futures extend gains: Oct contract RM4,427 (+RM29); Amspec says Oct 1-10 palm exports +37.73% to 491,954 tonnes
items.detail: Nov contract RM4,560 (+RM1), Dec RM4,700 (+RM18). Intertek reported Oct 1-10 exports +33.51% to 525,071 tonnes. Traders cite stronger early-October export demand and firmer energy prices for biodiesel feedstock demand, while record September stocks (3.51mil tonnes) still limit upside.
items.soWhat: Early-month export rebound helps prices, but stock overhang remains the ceiling.
items.opportunity: Short-window export strength into biodiesel demand if energy prices stay firm.
items.watchOut: Surveyor figures for Oct 1-10 only; September stock build still elevated.

items.headline: Salary Hero raises US$7.6mil Series A and enters Malaysia; targets 50 corporate partners by end-2027
items.detail: Bangkok earned-wage / financial-health platform; round led by Cento Ventures with Kairous Capital and M Venture Partners. Credit facility with regional lenders expanded to US$10mil. Operating in Malaysia since 2Q2026; Thailand base >100 companies and >300,000 employees.
items.soWhat: Another workplace lending model aiming at B40 households, adjacent to consumer-finance and cooperative channels.
items.opportunity: Employer payroll integrations as a distribution path versus traditional moneylenders.
items.watchOut: Early market entry; 50-partner target is a company forecast to end-2027.

items.headline: BNM: National Fraud Portal cut fund-tracing time by 75%; ~95% of scam cases are authorised push-payment fraud
items.detail: Assistant Governor Dr Norhana Endut said victims are often manipulated into approving payments, and instant payments shrink the intervention window. Portal automates reporting, tracing and recovery across payment networks; banks, telcos and platforms need shared intelligence.
items.soWhat: Consumer lenders and credit scorers remain exposed to sophisticated authorised fraud even as recovery tools improve.
items.watchOut: Cross-border and deepfake scams can still outrun domestic portals.
items.note: Remarks at IMF-World Bank meetings in Bangkok (Bernama via TMR).

items.headline: CRESS Acceleration Package SAC confirmed at 18 sen/kWh (from 14 sen); RE stocks fall up to 9.1% as analysts say UHV users may still save vs TNB
items.detail: Extra 4 sen/kWh borne by green electricity consumers, not developers. Conditions for the package still include min 10-year contract and COD by 31 Dec 2028; otherwise SAC stays 20 sen/kWh with three-year reviews. Illustrative total ~48 sen/kWh (30 sen solar + 18 sen SAC) vs TNB UHV peak 51.18 sen / off-peak 47.09 sen (ex-AFA). Yeo Bee Yin still seeking Petra/MITI/MOF clarification on the policy flip.
items.soWhat: Grid-access pricing is now a live risk for corporate RE that underpins DC power and cable/HV demand.
items.opportunity: If CRESS stays cheaper than TNB for UHV offtakers, DC RE build-out and related cable work can continue.
items.watchOut: Policy U-turn risk; some offtakers may reassess. HLIB notes still citing 14 sen are stale on this point.
items.note: Material update to the 14 Oct CRESS item: market now treating 18 sen as confirmed. MBSB Research and industry views labelled as such.

items.headline: Genting earmarks RM280mil of rights-issue working capital to pay interest costs; RM800mil still for debt repayment
items.detail: Reply to Bursa queries on the proposed RM1.25bil rights issue: RM280mil of the RM429.5mil working-capital slice for interest and financing costs; remaining RM149.5mil for general working capital. 25-30% TERP discount defended as needed to secure take-up. RM800mil debt repayment and RM20.5mil expenses unchanged.
items.soWhat: Confirms leverage pressure: a large slice of fresh equity is going straight to interest service.
items.watchOut: Still a proposal subject to approvals; dilution for minorities.
items.note: Material update to the 9 Oct rights-issue item.

items.headline: Gamuda Land opens ASAI Gamuda Cove, its first hotel: 280 rooms with Dusit International after 15 Sept pre-opening
items.detail: Official opening 10 Oct 2026 at Gamuda Cove, Selangor. Positioned to extend stays alongside the township's leisure, dining and commercial offer.
items.soWhat: A major developer is adding proprietary hotel inventory inside a township rather than only selling homes.
items.opportunity: Township leisure spend and longer visitor dwell time.
items.watchOut: Single-asset opening; no occupancy or ADR figures disclosed.

items.headline: Economist estimates haze costs Malaysia RM20mil-RM50mil a day (up to RM1.5bil a month); tourism arrivals could fall up to 8%
items.detail: Sunway University's Yeah Kim Leng: hardest-hit sectors tourism and aviation; palm yields may feel a 6-12 month lag; construction and logistics slowed. Public-health costs and productivity losses add to the bill. One KL hotel GM cited as estimating occupancy down 20-30% from a normal ~80% (single-property view).
items.soWhat: Haze is now a quantified near-term hit to hotel demand, not only flight cancellations.
items.watchOut: Estimates, not official statistics; one hotel occupancy anecdote is not industry data.
items.note: Economist/academic estimates. Single-hotel occupancy comment is anecdotal.

keyTakeaways.headline: DayOne's Johor book is still getting bigger — financing now about US$7.2bil
keyTakeaways.soWhat: After the earlier RM15bil bank top-up, DayOne says Malaysia financing is about US$7.2bil, with 1GW already billing and 2.3GW booked. That is the scale of funded DC work flowing to contractors, cables and power.

keyTakeaways.headline: CRESS at 18 sen is now market fact, and DC offtakers feel it
keyTakeaways.soWhat: After Tuesday's four-sen SAC lift, RE stocks fell as much as about 9%. Analysts argue UHV users may still beat TNB peak tariffs on an illustrative 48 sen vs 51.18 sen comparison, but the policy flip is exactly the investor-confidence risk Yeo flagged.

keyTakeaways.headline: Haze is hitting hotels and the wider economy in hard numbers
keyTakeaways.soWhat: An economist puts daily losses at RM20mil-RM50mil (up to RM1.5bil a month), with tourism arrivals at risk of an up-to-8% drop. That sits on top of Firefly's Subang-Seletar cancellations already flagged yesterday.

keyTakeaways.headline: Retail property finally has a story: CityWalk's AI reposition
keyTakeaways.soWhat: i-City's Savills mandate for the 180,000 sq ft CityWalk mall is a concrete retail-landlord move, pitched around AI/robotics and the i-Ris tower — while Battersea's RM1.52bil refinance keeps Malaysian developers active offshore.
